outcome: Matched delivery evidence shows whether the supported ExHarness product improves human effort and quality-adjusted cost.
currentProblem: Feasibility and architecture proofs do not establish that ExHarness is worth integrating into delivery.
constraints: Research must compare reuse and the smallest existing-Core approach, inspect primary sources and pin selected versions before READY.
Future dependency plans are assumptions, not delivered truth; worker execution requires delivered dependencies and a current Jev-satisfied plan.
Real-provider and live-product evidence must be identified separately from deterministic mocks; no fabricated API runs, costs or judgments.
successCriteria: At least the predeclared pilot sample is executed with equivalent direct-agent comparison and a held-out set; all attempts are recorded.
Quality and value gates fixed before the run are evaluated from raw evidence including failures/retries and human intervention.
A failed or inconclusive value gate yields an explicit no-go or follow-up scope; delivery cannot be claimed from selected successful demos.
